findings.reason: The protected source cleanly models legal stopping positions as a graph, precomputes all four roll endpoints with monotonic segment scans, and performs hash-set breadth-first search. Its rows, cols, segment_start, segment_end, stop-table, queue, and neighbor names expose the algorithm directly, so no inert candidate is materially justified.

Metadata consistently identifies Premium LeetCode problem 490 and its Python maze/start/destination Boolean contract. Search transitions only between complete-roll endpoints, so passing through the target cannot produce a false success. Two linear grid sweeps plus one graph traversal meet the manifest's O(rows * cols) time and space bounds.

The immutable native source is bound to verified submission 2065039081. It and the protected app source use identical horizontal and vertical segment scans, four endpoint tables, tuple conversion, deque search, dequeue-time target check, neighbor construction, visited-before-enqueue rule, and failure return. Differences are limited to the native class/type wrapper.

The disconnected-destination mazes contain 64, 256, and 1024 cells, span 16x, and force exhaustion of the reachable stopping graph after linear endpoint preprocessing. The protected source passed all 10 correctness cases and all three performance tiers, including the legal 100 by 100 boundary. A correct explicit linear-scan visited control passed every output but failed only the runtime verdict with relative growth exponent +0.19.

The current-targeted Approach exactly derives the stop-position graph, row and column segment endpoints, four precomputed tables, tuple queue, hash-set visitation, and dequeue-time success check. Its completeness argument distinguishes stopping from passing through, and its complexity accounts for preprocessing, search, and all stored tables.

The hash-bound modular Reference was checked directly against the authenticated Premium statement. It preserves rolling-until-wall semantics, border-wall assumption, exact-stop requirement, all three examples and the first two explanations, all ten constraints, and source section order. Both source images were independently recreated as accessible tables with the same maze, start, destination, and wall relationships.

coverage: All three authenticated Premium source examples now appear first and in source order with their exact mazes, start and destination coordinates, and Boolean results. The third source example was restored and the invented open-center case was relabelled as a trial.

The illegal same-cell fixture was removed. Every case now honors the guarantees that start and destination are distinct in-bounds empty cells in a rectangular binary maze with at least two empty spaces.

Boundaries cover 1 by 2 and 2 by 1 minimum mazes, a legal 100 by 100 maximum maze, row and column coordinates 0 and 99, walls and open cells, straight rolls, turns, isolated regions, open corners, and a center cell where the ball cannot stop.

An independent direct-roll breadth-first oracle verified all ten correctness cases and all three benchmark outputs, 10,252 exhaustive small-maze routes, and 1,000 randomized routes. The protected implementation agreed throughout.
All ten correctness cases are visible samples or trials; the unchanged 64-, 256-, and 1024-cell workloads remain hidden and performance-only in benchmark.json.
